course.title: AP Precalculus
course.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
course.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

variants.stem: The graph of r = 6 − 6 cos θ is a cardioid.

parts.prompt: What is the largest value of r?
What is the smallest value of r?
For which θ with 0 ≤ θ < 2π is r = 0?

solution: cos θ ranges from −1 to 1, so r = 6 − 6 cos θ ranges from 6 − 6 = 0 to 6 + 6 = 12. The largest value is 12.
The smallest value is 0, so the curve touches the origin.
r = 0 when cos θ = 1, which happens at θ = 0 for 0 ≤ θ < 2π.

variants.stem: Use each equation to describe its polar graph.

parts.prompt: How many petals does the graph of r = 8 sin(6θ) have?
What kind of graph is r = 1 − 3 cos θ?
What kind of graph is r = 3 − 3 cos θ?

solution: This is a rose r = a sin(nθ) with n = 6. When n is even, the rose has 2n petals, so it has 12 petals.
The coefficient 3 of cos θ is greater than the constant 1, so r becomes negative for some θ. That makes a limaçon with an inner loop.
The constant 3 equals the size of the coefficient of cos θ, which is 3, so the graph is a cardioid.

variants.stem: Consider the polar function r = −4 sin(2θ) with π ≤ θ ≤ 3π/2.

parts.prompt: Is r positive or negative on this interval?
In which quadrant are the points of the graph on this interval?
Find the point of this part of the graph that is farthest from the origin. Give its distance |r| and its θ.

solution: On π ≤ θ ≤ 3π/2, 2θ goes from 2π to 3π, where sin(2θ) is positive. With the coefficient −4, r is negative.
Because r is negative, the points are opposite the angles θ. The angles are in Quadrant III, so the points are in Quadrant I.
|sin(2θ)| = 1 when 2θ = 5π/2, that is, θ = 5π/4. There |r| = 4.

variants.stem: The polar graph of r = a + b cos θ, where a and b are positive numbers, is shown. Point A is the point of the graph where θ = 0, and point B is the point of the graph where θ = π.

stimulusBlocks.caption: The graph of r = a + b cos θ with points A (θ = 0) and B (θ = π)
stimulusBlocks.alt: A polar grid with a closed curve. Point A is on the positive x-axis, 7 units from the origin. Point B is on the negative x-axis, 1 unit from the origin.

parts.prompt: Find r at point A.
Find r at point B. Remember that r is negative when B is on the opposite side of the origin from the ray θ = π.
Find a and b.
What kind of graph is this?

solution: A is 7 units from the origin on the positive x-axis, and r is positive there, so r = 7.
B is 1 unit from the origin on the negative x-axis, which is the ray θ = π, so r = 1.
At θ = 0, r = a + b = 7. At θ = π, r = a − b = 1. Adding gives 2a = 8, so a = 4, and b = 7 − 4 = 3.
Because a > b, r is never negative, so the graph is a limaçon without an inner loop.

variants.stem: The sensitivity of a microphone to sound arriving from an angle θ, measured from the front of the microphone, is r = 8 + 6 cos θ.

parts.prompt: What is the greatest sensitivity?

solution: cos θ is at most 1, so the greatest sensitivity is 8 + 6 = 14, at θ = 0.
